children.comment: Meet the d-pawn with the d-pawn. You claim the centre and get a solid, simple game.
White attacks d5 from the side.
This is the Slav. It is your Caro-Kann pawn move: ...c6 guards d5 and keeps your c8 bishop free.
White develops and guards d4.
Develop and guard d5 again. In the main line your plan is ...dxc4, then ...Bf5, then ...e6.
Take the pawn on c4. While your b7 pawn is at home, bring the bishop out before you play ...e6.
White stops ...b5 and plans e3 and Bxc4.
Bring the bishop out before ...e6, as in the Caro-Kann. The pawn on a4 stops ...b5, so do not try to keep the c4 pawn.
Now the bishop is outside your pawns. This is your Caro-Kann plan: bishop first, then ...e6.
White wins the pawn back.
Pin the knight on c3 against the king. Next you play ...Nbd7 and castle.
Develop the last knight. It supports the later breaks ...e5 and ...c5. Then you castle.
Step back before e3-e4 can hit the bishop on f5. On g6 it also watches the e4 square.
Castle. Your king is safe and your pieces are out. Aim for ...e5 or ...c5 later, like in the Caro-Kann.
White puts the bishop on d3. It guards the e4 pawn, which blocks its diagonal to your g6 bishop.
Put the rook on the e-file. It prepares the ...e5 break, a Caro-Kann idea you know.
White puts the rook behind the bishop on d3.
Break with ...e5. The pawn attacks d4, and your rook on e8 guards it.
White takes the pawn. White's new e5 pawn attacks your f6 knight.
Retake with the d7 knight. It now attacks the bishop on d3 and the knight on f3.
White trades knights. The white knight on e5 has no guard, so you can take it.
Take with the rook. It stands in the centre, and no white pawn attacks it yet.
White pushes the e-pawn. It attacks your f6 knight.
Trade bishops: the d3 bishop now looks at your g6 bishop. Your f6 knight can wait, because exf6 loses the queen to ...Bxe2.
White retakes with the queen. The e5 pawn still attacks your f6 knight.
Move the knight to d5. The c6 and e6 pawns guard it, and it attacks the knight on c3.
White trades on d5. That knight also attacks your bishop on b4, so retake at once.
Retake with the c-pawn. You get a pawn on d5, and the c-file is open.
White attacks your c4 pawn with the knight.
Challenge the knight. Your c4 pawn has no guard, so White can take it back.
White takes the pawn back with the knight.
Bring the queen to c7. It will guard a pawn on e5 when you play ...e5.
White's pawn on g3 blocks the c7-h2 diagonal and makes room for the bishop on g2.
Strike in the centre with ...e5. The queen on c7 and the knight on d7 both guard it.
White takes on e5. The pawn attacks your f6 knight.
Retake with the d7 knight. It attacks the c4 knight, and nothing guards that knight.
The bishop attacks your e5 knight. Your queen on c7 stands behind that knight.
The e5 knight is attacked twice, by the bishop and by the c4 knight. Bring the f6 knight to d7 to guard it a second time.
White wants to take back on c4 with the bishop.
Hold the pawn with ...b5. The c6 pawn guards b5, so the pawn is safe.
Push the pawn. It attacks the knight on c3 and wins space.
Open the f8 bishop and guard d5. Then you can bring the c8 bishop out with ...Bb7 or ...Ba6.
White takes back the c4 pawn. Your b-pawn moved to b4, so nothing guarded c4.
Develop the c8 bishop. The c6 pawn blocks it for now, but a later ...c5 will open its diagonal.
White castles.
Develop the f8 bishop. Now f8 and g8 are free, so you can castle.
White's queen steps to e2 and guards the bishop on c4.
Castle. Your king sits behind the f7, g7 and h7 pawns.
White builds a big centre.
Hold the pawn with ...b5 at once. The c6 pawn guards it.
White pushes the e-pawn. It attacks your f6 knight.
Move the knight to d5. The c6 pawn guards it, and it attacks the knight on c3.
White attacks your b5 pawn with the a-pawn.
Guard the d5 knight again with the e-pawn and open the f8 bishop.
White takes on b5. Your c4 pawn is no longer guarded by a pawn on b5.
Take the c3 knight first. After bxc3 your c6 pawn takes back on b5.
White retakes with the b-pawn.
Retake on b5. The b5 pawn guards your c4 pawn, and you are a pawn up.
White plans to win the c4 pawn back with the knight.
Challenge the knight at once. If it takes on d7, you retake.
White takes the c4 pawn back with the knight.
Hit the knight with the b-pawn. The c6 pawn guards b5, so White must move the knight.
White's knight goes back to e5. It attacks your c6 pawn and your d7 knight, and nothing guards c6.
Take the knight. After dxe5 you can trade queens on d1 before your f6 knight is taken.
White retakes. The e5 pawn attacks your f6 knight, and the queens face each other on the open d-file.
Take the queen with check. After White retakes, it is your move, so your f6 knight can leave.
White retakes with the king. The king can no longer castle.
Move the knight to g4. It attacks the pawns on e5 and f2, and nothing guards either one.
White's king goes back to e1 and guards f2. The e5 pawn still has no guard.
Take the e5 pawn. You are a pawn up, and White cannot castle.
White retreats the knight to e3. The b5 pawn does not attack that square.
Develop the bishop. The c6 pawn blocks it for now, but a later ...c5 will open its diagonal.
White prepares to put the bishop on g2.
Guard d5 and open the f8 bishop.
White's bishop attacks your c6 pawn along the long diagonal. Your b7 bishop guards that pawn.
Put the queen on b6. It attacks the d4 pawn, which only the white queen guards.
White castles.
Develop the f8 bishop so you can castle next.
Same idea as in the Caro-Kann: bishop out before ...e6.
Now the bishop is outside your pawns. Solid and calm.
The knight attacks your bishop on f5.
Step back. If White takes on g6, retake with the h-pawn: your h8 rook gets the half-open h-file.
White takes your bishop. Retake with the h-pawn.
Retake with the h-pawn. Your h8 rook now sees the h2 pawn along the half-open h-file.
White develops the bishop.
Develop the b8 knight. It guards the f6 knight and supports ...c5 and ...e5.
White takes on d5. You can retake with the e-pawn or the c-pawn.
Retake with the e-pawn. The c6 pawn and the f6 knight both guard d5.
Develop and guard d5. Next comes ...e6 or ...dxc4.
Solid: ...e6 guards d5 and opens the f8 bishop. The c8 bishop is shut in, but ...dxc4 and ...b5 free it later.
Develop the knight to d7. It supports ...c5 and ...e5 later, and it keeps ...dxc4 ready.
Take on c4 and gain time: your pawn attacks the bishop on d3.
Push the pawn. It attacks the bishop on c4 and gains space.
Guard the b5 pawn with ...a6. Now the b5 pawn is solid.
Strike the centre with ...c5. It is the same break as in the Caro-Kann.
White attacks your f6 knight with the e-pawn.
Take on d4. The pawn attacks the knight on c3, while White's e5 pawn attacks your f6 knight.
White takes the b5 pawn, but your a6 pawn attacks the knight.
Take the knight with the a-pawn. White's e5 pawn still attacks your f6 knight.
White takes your f6 knight. You can retake with the g-pawn, the queen or the d7 knight.
Retake with the g-pawn. The f6 pawn controls e5 and g5, and the g-file is half-open for your rooks.
White castles. Your b5 and d4 pawns are both attacked.
Guard both pawns with one move. The queen defends b5 and d4.
White's queen backs up the bishop on d3, which attacks your b5 pawn.
Push the pawn to b4. The bishop on d3 no longer attacks it, and your queen guards it from b6.
White puts the queen on c2. It supports the c3 knight and attacks the h7 pawn along the diagonal.
Develop the bishop to d6, where it aims at the h2 pawn. Now f8 is free, so you can castle.
The bishop joins the queen. Both now aim at your h7 pawn.
Castle. The f6 knight and the king both guard h7.
White castles.
Take on c4. The pawn attacks the bishop on d3, but White can take it back.
White takes the pawn back.
Attack the bishop with the b-pawn. Nothing guards the bishop on c4.
White's bishop goes back to d3.
Free the c8 bishop through b7, now that the b-pawn has moved. A later ...c5 will open its diagonal.
Same position as the main Slav, so take the pawn and follow your plan.
The Exchange Slav. White trades pawns and the game becomes symmetrical.
Retake with the c-pawn. You have a pawn in the centre and an open c-file.
Develop and guard d5.
Develop with pressure on d4. This knight also supports a later ...e5.
Bring the bishop out before ...e6, as in the Caro-Kann.
Now the bishop is outside your pawns. You are solid and well developed.
Trade your good bishop for theirs. Then ...Bb4 pins the knight.
Pin the knight on c3 against the king. Then castle.
White castles. Your bishop no longer pins the c3 knight to the king.
Castle. Now all your minor pieces are developed, and your king sits behind the f7, g7 and h7 pawns.
White puts a rook on the open c-file, behind the c3 knight.
Trade the bishop for the c3 knight. That knight controls e4, so your f6 knight can jump there next.
White retakes with the rook.
Put the knight on e4, where your d5 pawn guards it. It attacks the rook on c3.
The rook goes back to c1.
Attack the b2 pawn with the queen. Nothing guards it now.
White's queen attacks your b7 pawn and your d5 pawn.
Attack the queen with the knight. The knight on a5 also guards b7.
White's queen gives check along the a4-e8 diagonal and attacks your a5 knight.
Block the check with the bishop. The bishop attacks the queen on a4.
White's queen retreats to c2.
Guard d5 and open the f8 bishop.
White develops the knight.
Put the rook on the open c-file. The white queen and the c3 knight stand on that file.
White develops the bishop.
Pin the c3 knight to the king on e1. Your rook on c8 also attacks that knight.
Develop and guard d5. You will play ...e6 or ...Bf5 next.
Solid: ...e6 guards d5 and opens the f8 bishop.
Develop the knight to d7. Same set-up as in the line with 3.Nc3.
Bring the bishop out before ...e6. Same idea as the Caro-Kann.
This is the London-style bishop move. It comes out before White’s e-pawn moves.
Strike at d4 at once. Bf4 left c1, so only the queen guards d4. This is the Caro-Kann ...c5 break you know.
White guards d4 with the e-pawn.
Attack d4 a second time. Develop with a purpose.
White adds another guard on d4 with the c-pawn.
Hit b2. The bishop left c1, so nothing guards that pawn. An early queen move is fine when it makes a threat.
White guards b2 and offers a queen trade.
Push the pawn. It attacks the queen on b3 and gains space.
Retake with the a-pawn. Your rook can use the a-file, and the doubled b-pawns are fine.
Bring the knight out. Next you play ...Bf5, the Caro-Kann bishop move.
White's a3 pawn attacks the b4 square.
Guard the c4 pawn and gain space on the queenside.
White develops the bishop.
Bring the c8 bishop out before ...e6, like in the Caro-Kann.
White brings the g1 knight to f3.
Play ...e6 now that the bishop is outside the pawns. The e6 pawn guards the bishop on f5 and the d5 pawn.
White castles.
Develop the f8 bishop and get ready to castle.
White guards b2 with the queen.
Bishop out before ...e6. White’s queen on c1 guards b2, so you develop instead.
White leaves b2 loose.
Bishop out before ...e6. Nd2 does not guard b2, so ...Qxb2 is still possible. If Qb3, trade queens.
Develop your knight. After White plays c3, you play ...Qb6.
Hit b2. With Nf3 and Bf4 out, nothing guards that pawn.
White guards b2 and offers a queen trade.
Push the pawn. It attacks the queen on b3 and gains space.
Retake with the a-pawn. Your rook can use the a-file, and the doubled b-pawns are fine.
Guard the c4 pawn and gain space. Your queenside pawns are strong now.
White guards b2 with the queen.
Bishop out before ...e6. The queen on c1 guards b2, so go back to development.
Take on d4. After exd4 your bishop comes out to f5.
Bishop out before ...e6. Then ...e6 and ...Nf6 finish your development.
White takes a pawn.
Strike with ...e5 at once. It attacks the bishop on f4, and you win the pawn back after it moves.
White's bishop steps back to g3 because your e5 pawn attacked it.
Take the pawn back with the f8 bishop. It also attacks the e3 pawn.
White develops the knight and attacks your e5 pawn.
Your e5 pawn is attacked twice, by the knight and by the bishop. The f6 pawn gives it a second guard.
White attacks d5 with the c-pawn.
Push the pawn to d4. The bishop on c5, the knight on c6, the e5 pawn and the queen all guard it.
White takes on d4. The new pawn attacks your c5 bishop and your e5 pawn.
Take on d4 with the knight. That removes the pawn that attacked your bishop, and the knight attacks the f3 knight.
White pins your knight to the king.
Break the pin. Then you can take on d4 or play ...a6.
White develops the knight and guards d4.
Develop the g8 knight, which guards d5 and the d7 bishop. If White takes on c5, ...e6 and ...Bxc5 win the pawn back.
White castles.
Guard d5 and open the f8 bishop.
White develops the b1 knight.
Develop the f8 bishop so you can castle next.
White guards d4 with the c-pawn.
Attack d4 again. Now d4 has two attackers.
Hit b2. White played c3 and e3, but nothing guards b2.
Develop your knight. You still plan ...Qb6.
Hit b2. Neither the knight on f3 nor the c3 pawn guards it.
The knight blocks White’s own queen from d4.
Take on d4. After cxd4 Nxd4 you win a pawn, and Nd2 blocks the queen. If e3 hits the knight, retreat to c6.
White takes a pawn.
Strike with ...e5. It attacks the bishop on f4, and you win the pawn back.
White takes the pawn.
Open the f8 bishop. Next you play ...Bxc5 and win the pawn back.
Take the pawn back. You develop and keep an equal game.
Develop your knight and guard d5. Castle soon.
White hits d5 with the c-pawn.
Develop the b8 knight. It controls d4 and e5.
White develops the knight.
Castle. Your bishop left f8 and your knight left g8, so you can castle now.
White's a3 pawn attacks the b4 square.
Put the rook on e8, behind the e6 pawn. It will guard that pawn if you play ...e5.
White’s queen comes out early.
Develop with a threat. The knight attacks the queen on d4.
White develops and guards d4.
Attack d4 a second time and develop.
Develop your knight. You still plan ...Qb6.
Hit b2. The c3 and e3 pawns do not guard it, and the bishop left c1.
Develop and guard d5. Most set-ups from here share your Caro-Kann ideas.
Bring the bishop out before ...e6. It is the Caro-Kann move you know.
White offers to trade your bishop.
Trade bishops. Your bishop got out first, so the trade costs you nothing.
Prepare ...e6 and ...Nbd7. This is the Slav and Caro-Kann pawn shape again.
Close the centre solidly. Your set-up is complete: ...c6, ...d5, ...e6.
Develop the last knight. Next you play ...Be7 and castle.
Close the centre. Your set-up is solid, and White has doubled d-pawns on d3 and d4.
White hits d5 from the side.
Guard d5 with the c-pawn. You reach the Slav with your bishop already out.
Solid. The bishop is outside your pawns, and d5 is well guarded.
The knight attacks your bishop.
Nh4 attacks your bishop. Move it and attack their queen: Bg4.
White hits d5 from the side.
Guard d5 with the c-pawn. You reach the Slav. Follow the Slav plan: ...dxc4, ...Bf5, ...e6.
Strike at d4 with the c-pawn. This is the anti-London plan: ...c5, ...Nc6, ...Qb6.
Attack d4 a second time and develop.
Hit b2. Same plan as against 2.Bf4: nothing guards that pawn.
The bishop eyes your knight.
Hit the bishop with the knight. If Bf4, you play ...c5 at once.
Strike at d4 with the c-pawn, like in the anti-London line.
Guard d5 with the c-pawn and prepare ...Bf5.
Bring the bishop out before ...e6.
Develop and guard d5. You will play ...Bf5 next.
Bring the bishop out before ...e6. It is the Caro-Kann move you know.
Trade it. Then you play ...c6 and ...e6.
The Slav and Caro-Kann pawn shape again: ...c6 and ...d5.
White develops the bishop before the knight.
Hit d4 with the c-pawn. It is the same break as in the Caro-Kann.
Attack d4 a second time and develop.
White develops the bishop early.
Strike at d4. If White plays e3, answer with ...Qb6.
Hit b2. After Nc3, play ...e6. Do not grab b2.
Guard d5 and open the f8 bishop. The b2 pawn looks free, but taking it is risky.
A gambit: White offers a pawn.
Take the pawn. Give it back later if you must, but get your pieces out first.
Develop and guard your extra pawn on e4. You are a pawn up, so finish your development.
Take again. Then play ...Bf5 or ...e6 and finish your development.
Develop and guard d5.
Guard d5 and stop Nb5. You will play ...Bf5 next.
Bishop out before ...e6. Your c6 pawn already stops Nb5.

Claim the centre. Same pawns as the Slav.
Develop and guard d5. You are in the Slav. Play ...dxc4, ...Bf5, ...e6.
Develop and guard d5. Next comes ...e6 and ...Nbd7.
White attacks d5 a second time.
Guard d5 with the e-pawn and open the f8 bishop. The e6 pawn blocks your c8 bishop for now; ...b5, ...Bb7 and later ...c5 can free it.
White puts a pawn on d4 and claims the centre.
Develop the b8 knight. It guards the f6 knight and supports ...c5 and ...e5.
White's bishop guards the c4 pawn.
Take on c4. The pawn attacks the bishop on d3, but White can take it back.
White takes the pawn back.
Attack the bishop with ...b5. It gains space, and nothing guards the bishop on c4.

Free the c8 bishop through b7, now that the b-pawn has moved. A later ...c5 will open its diagonal.

Retake with the c-pawn. If cxd5 follows, you can win the pawn back with ...Nf6 and ...Nxd5.
Develop and attack the d5 pawn. You plan to win it back.
Take the pawn back. Your knight is active in the centre.
White develops the bishop. The knight on d5 is attacked twice, by the bishop and by the c3 knight, and guarded once.
Retreat the knight with an attack on the c4 bishop.
White's bishop retreats to b3. It still aims at the f7 pawn.
Develop the b8 knight. It controls d4 and e5.
White develops the knight and guards d4.
Bring the c8 bishop out before ...e6, like in the Caro-Kann.
White takes the centre.
Now the bishop is outside your pawns. The e6 pawn guards it and the d5 square, and it opens the f8 bishop.
White castles.
Develop the f8 bishop so you can castle next.

White prepares to put the bishop on g2.

Now the bishop is outside your pawns. The e6 pawn guards d5 and opens the f8 bishop.
White guards the c4 pawn and makes room for the c1 bishop on b2.
